captions: 3:52 p.m. On the way to the gym. His story, again.
New car. New flat. Same age as you.
You pocket the phone. Your chest feels tight.
On the treadmill, you replay it in your head.
Next to you, an old man walks slowly. A brace on one leg.
He catches your eye and smiles: “Alhamdulillah, I can walk today.”
Your legs are running. You never once counted that.
Walking home, you count yours. Legs. Lungs. A mum who calls.
Then the hardest part: a du'a for him.
And the tightness in your chest lets go.

post.caption:
14 times you replayed his story. Not once did you thank Allah. 🤍

Comparison steals what you already have. An old man on a treadmill reminded me: some people pray just to walk.

“And what is the worldly life except the enjoyment of delusion.” (57:20)

Before Maghrib: make du'a for him. Then thank Allah for yours.
